title_en: Dongfang Company, Guangzhou Office v. Zhongshan Industrial Raw Materials Company, et al. — dispute over a loan guarantee contract
ruling_gist_en: For evidence provided by the parties during the second instance, the people's court may decide whether to conduct cross-examination based on the specific circumstances of the case. Evidence that has been cross-examined can serve as the basis for finding facts.
keywords_en: Civil; Dispute over loan guarantee contract; Second instance; Supreme People's Court; Guangdong Province; Legal person; Financial institution; Contract Law; Guarantee Law; Whether the loan was actually disbursed; Whether the statute of limitations was interrupted; Whether guarantee liability is established; Partial support; Loan contract; Joint and several liability guarantee; Assignment of creditor's rights; Collection notice; Contract dispute; Guarantee; Loan guarantee contract dispute involving Liao Company, et al.
full_text_en:
Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office v. Zhongshan Industrial Raw Materials Company et al. — Dispute over Loan Guarantee Contract

Ruling Summary

With respect to evidence submitted by the parties during the second instance, the People's Court may decide on the method of examination of evidence based on the specific circumstances of the case. Evidence that has been examined may serve as the basis for determining the facts of the case.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2004) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 207

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): China Orient Asset Management Corporation, Guangzhou Office. Domicile: 17/F, East Tower, International Financial Building, No. 197 Dongfeng West Road, Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province.

Responsible Person: Zhang Ziai, General Manager of the Office.

Agent ad litem: Li Guangming, Staff Member of the Office.

Agent ad litem: Ji Xianghong, Attorney at Beijing Bohan Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Zhongshan Industrial Raw Materials Company. Domicile: Jinghua Hotel, Zhongshan No. 3 Road, Zhongshan City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Lu Lünan, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Xiongwei, Attorney at Guangdong Gongliang Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: He Siping, Attorney at Guangdong Gongliang Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Zhongshan Urban and Rural Construction Development Corporation. Domicile: No. 23 Huabo Road, Zhongshan City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Li Runqiang, General Manager of the Corporation.

Agent ad litem: Li Qianmei, Attorney at Guangdong Zhongyuan Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Chi, Attorney at Guangdong Zhongyuan Law Firm.

The appellant, China Orient Asset Management Corporation, Guangzhou Office (hereinafter referred to as the Guangzhou Office), appealed to the Supreme People's Court against the civil judgment (2004) Yue Gao Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 1 rendered by the Guangdong High People's Court in the case of a dispute over a loan guarantee contract between it and the appellees, Zhongshan Industrial Raw Materials Company (hereinafter referred to as the Raw Materials Company) and Zhongshan Urban and Rural Construction Development Corporation (hereinafter referred to as the Construction Corporation). This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel composed of Presiding Judge Xu Ruibai, Judge Zhang Shuming, and Acting Judge Wang Xiansen to hear the case. The court clerk, Pan Yongfeng, served as the recorder. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

The facts found by the court of first instance are as follows:

On December 21, 1995, the Bank of China, Zhongshan Branch (hereinafter referred to as Zhongshan BOC) entered into two foreign exchange loan contracts with the Raw Materials Company. The contracts stipulated that the Raw Materials Company would borrow USD 2,000,000 and USD 1,250,000 respectively from Zhongshan BOC; the loan term for both was 12 months; the interest rate for the loans was 7.5% per annum for foreign exchange loans, subject to adjustment in accordance with the provisions of the Head Office of the Bank of China if the national interest rate was adjusted. On the same day, the Construction Corporation issued two letters of guarantee to Zhongshan BOC, undertaking to provide joint and several liability guarantees for the above two loans. The scope of the guarantee was the principal and interest of the USD 2,000,000 and USD 1,250,000 loans and any expenses incurred, and the guarantee period was until the borrower had repaid all the principal and interest in full. After the said contracts were signed, Zhongshan BOC transferred a total of USD 3,250,000 in two tranches to the Raw Materials Company on the same day. The Raw Materials Company affixed its seal to the loan receipt to confirm receipt of the said loans.

On May 7, 1996, the Raw Materials Company submitted a report to Zhongshan BOC, applying for a loan of USD 1,611,031.25. Subsequently, the two parties entered into another foreign exchange loan contract. The contract stipulated that the Raw Materials Company would borrow USD 1,611,031.25 from Zhongshan BOC, but did not specify the loan term, interest rate, or specific date of signing. On May 18 of the same year, the Construction Corporation submitted an irrevocable letter of guarantee to Zhongshan BOC, undertaking to provide joint and several liability guarantees for the said loan, with the guarantee period until the borrower had repaid all the principal and interest of the said loan in full. During the trial of the first instance, the Guangzhou Office claimed that Zhongshan BOC had disbursed USD 1,611,031.25 to the Raw Materials Company immediately after the signing of the said loan contract, but the Guangzhou Office failed to provide corresponding evidence of the transfer. The Raw Materials Company, on the other hand, stated that the said loan had not been disbursed.

After the loan terms expired, the Raw Materials Company failed to repay the loan principal and interest. On September 29, 1999, Zhongshan BOC issued a Notice of Demand for Overdue Loans to the Raw Materials Company and the Construction Corporation respectively, requiring the Raw Materials Company to repay the principal and interest of the loans, including the three loans in question, within 7 working days, and requiring the Construction Corporation, as the guarantor for these three loans, to urge the borrower to repay the loans within 7 working days. The amount of the third loan recorded in the Notice of Demand for Overdue Loans issued by Zhongshan BOC to the Raw Materials Company was not the USD 1,611,031.25 stipulated in the loan contract, but was recorded as USD 1,611,000, with a loan term from December 27, 1996 to December 26, 1997. The Raw Materials Company and the Construction Corporation, in their capacities as borrower and guarantor respectively, affixed their seals to the said notices to confirm receipt.

On April 29, 2000, Zhongshan BOC and the Guangzhou Office entered into three separate agreements for the assignment of creditor's rights, stipulating that Zhongshan BOC would assign to the Guangzhou Office the creditor's rights to the principal and interest of the above three loans. On June 18 of the same year, Zhongshan BOC sent a notice of assignment of creditor's rights to the Raw Materials Company by mail, requiring the Raw Materials Company to repay the loan principal and interest to the Guangzhou Office. The Guangdong Provincial Notary Office issued a notarial certificate on June 29 of the same year to notarize the above facts. On September 22 of the same year, the Guangzhou Office mailed to the Construction Corporation, the guarantor, a notice jointly issued by the Guangzhou Office and Zhongshan BOC regarding the assignment of creditor's rights and demand for payment. The Guangdong Provincial Notary Office issued a notarial certificate on September 29 of the same year to notarize the above facts. On March 15, 2002, the Guangzhou Office published a notice demanding payment of creditor's rights in the Nanfang Daily, demanding payment from the relevant debtors and guarantors, including demand for payment of the principal and interest of the three loans in question from the Raw Materials Company and the Construction Corporation. On November 25, 2002, the Guangzhou Office sent by mail a notice demanding payment of the three loans in question to the guarantor, the Construction Corporation. The Guangdong Provincial Notary Office issued a notarial certificate on December 12 of the same year to notarize the above facts. On January 30, 2003, the Guangzhou Office again published a notice demanding payment of creditor's rights in the Nanfang Daily, demanding payment from the relevant debtors and guarantors, which also included demand for payment of the principal and interest of the three loans in question from the Raw Materials Company and the Construction Corporation. On December 1, 2003, the Guangzhou Office sent by mail a notice demanding payment of loan principal and interest to the debtor, the Raw Materials Company, and the guarantor, the Construction Corporation. Since the above amounts were not repaid, the Guangzhou Office filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, requesting a judgment ordering the Raw Materials Company to repay the loan principal of USD 4,861,031.25 (equivalent to RMB 40,239,616.69) and interest accrued up to December 31, 2003 in the amount of USD 5,245,718.75 (equivalent to RMB 43,424,063.56), as well as liquidated damages for overdue payment in the amount of RMB 16,521,384.58; and ordering the Construction Corporation to bear joint and several liability for the above debts.

The court of first instance held that: The loan contracts in this case entered into between Zhongshan BOC and the Raw Materials Company reflected the true intentions of the parties, the contents of the contracts were lawful, and they should be deemed lawful and valid. The disputed issue in this case is whether the loan of USD 1,611,031.25 was actually disbursed. The loan contract for USD 1,611,031.25 entered into by the parties did not include the date of signing of the contract, the date of loan disbursement, the loan term, the interest rate, and other terms. Nor could the Guangzhou Office provide evidence of the transfer or loan receipt for the disbursement of the loan. Moreover, the Raw Materials Company denied having received the loan. The report submitted by the Raw Materials Company to Zhongshan BOC on May 7, 1996 applying for a loan could only prove that the Raw Materials Company applied for a loan of USD 1,611,031.25, but could not prove that the Raw Materials Company had actually received the loan. The Guangzhou Office alleged that the amounts demanded in the Notice of Demand for Overdue Loans dated September 29, 1999 included the loan of USD 1,611,031.25, but the amount recorded in that notice was USD 1,611,000, and the loan term for that amount was from December 27, 1996 to December 26, 1997, which did not match the date of the alleged loan of USD 1,611,031.25, which the Guangzhou Office claimed occurred on May 18, 1996. Therefore, the said notice could not prove that the loan of USD 1,611,031.25 had been disbursed. Although the assignment of creditor's rights agreement entered into by the Guangzhou Office and Zhongshan BOC on April 29, 2000, and the subsequent notice of assignment of creditor's rights, included the loan of USD 1,611,031.25, since the agreement and the notice were unilateral acts by the creditor and were not confirmed by the Raw Materials Company, they could not prove that the loan had actually been made. Accordingly, the Guangzhou Office's claim for the Raw Materials Company to repay the loan of USD 1,611,031.25 was not supported due to insufficient evidence.

With respect to the two loan contracts signed on December 21, 1995, Zhongshan BOC disbursed a total of USD 3,250,000 in two tranches to the Raw Materials Company on the day the contracts were signed, and the Raw Materials Company also acknowledged receipt of the said amounts. The repayment term for the USD 3,250,000 loan was December 21, 1996. Within two years from the expiry of that term, there was no evidence to show that any statutory ground for the interruption of the statute of limitations had occurred. Therefore, the creditor's right for the USD 3,250,000 loan had exceeded the statute of limitations as of December 21, 1998. On September 29, 1999, the Raw Materials Company affixed its seal to the notice of demand issued by Zhongshan BOC to confirm the debt, which constituted a new confirmation of the loan debt after the expiry of the statute of limitations, and the statute of limitations period should be recalculated. The said notice of demand required the Raw Materials Company to repay the debt within 7 working days after receipt of the notice, meaning that the statute of limitations for the loan should be recalculated from 7 working days after September 29, 1999. On April 29, 2000, the Guangzhou Office and Zhongshan BOC entered into two agreements for the assignment of creditor's rights, stipulating that Zhongshan BOC would assign the creditor's rights for the two loans totaling USD 3,250,000 to the Guangzhou Office. The notice of assignment of the above creditor's rights was mailed to the Raw Materials Company after notarization on June 18, 2000. The assignment of creditor's rights complied with the provisions of Articles 79 and 80 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China and was legally binding on the debtor, the Raw Materials Company. The said notice of assignment of creditor's rights contained a demand that the debtor, the Raw Materials Company, repay the loan principal and interest to the assignee of the creditor's rights, the Guangzhou Office. This act constituted an exercise of rights by the creditor against the debtor, and since it occurred within the two-year statute of limitations period, it constituted an interruption of the statute of limitations. After the interruption of the statute of limitations for the USD 3,250,000 loan creditor's right on June 18, 2000, the creditor, the Guangzhou Office, published notices demanding payment of creditor's rights in the Nanfang Daily on March 15, 2002 and January 30, 2003, and sent a notice demanding payment to the Raw Materials Company by mail on December 1, 2003. All of the above acts constituted exercises of rights by the creditor within the two-year statute of limitations period. Pursuant to Article 10 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases Involving Assets Formed from the Acquisition, Management, and Disposal of Non-performing Loans of State-owned Banks by Financial Asset Management Companies, the above acts all constituted interruptions of the statute of limitations. Therefore, the creditor's right for the USD 3,250,000 loan had not exceeded the statute of limitations, and the Raw Materials Company should repay the principal, interest, and overdue penalty interest for the USD 3,250,000 loan to the Guangzhou Office.

The Construction Corporation issued two letters of guarantee to Zhongshan BOC on December 21, 1995, undertaking to provide joint and several liability guarantees for the USD 3,250,000 loan. The guarantee should be deemed lawful and valid. The guarantee dispute in this case should be governed by the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China and the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China. The guarantee period stipulated in the letters of guarantee was until the borrower had repaid all the loan principal and interest. In accordance with the second paragraph of Article 32 of the above judicial interpretation, the guarantee period should be determined as two years after the maturity of the principal debt, i.e., the guarantee period for the Construction Corporation's guarantee for the two loans was two years after December 21, 1996. In this case, there is no evidence to show that Zhongshan BOC exercised its rights against the guarantor within the above guarantee period. Therefore, the Construction Corporation could be exempted from the guarantee liability. On September 29, 1999, the Construction Corporation affixed its seal to the notice issued by Zhongshan BOC demanding that it assume the guarantee liability. This constituted a new provision of a guarantee for the debt after the expiry of the guarantee period, and a new guarantee relationship was thus formed between the parties. Since the parties did not stipulate a guarantee period, in accordance with the first paragraph of Article 32 of the above judicial interpretation, the guarantee period should be determined as six months after the maturity of the principal debt, i.e., six months from 7 working days after September 29, 1999. After the Guangzhou Office acquired the creditor's rights, it sent a notice demanding payment to the Construction Corporation by mail on September 22, 2000. By that time, the guarantee period had already expired, and the Construction Corporation did not provide a new guarantee. Therefore, the Construction Corporation would no longer bear the guarantee liability. The subsequent acts of the Guangzhou Office in publishing a demand notice in the Nanfang Daily on March 15, 2002, sending a demand notice to the Construction Corporation by mail on November 25, 2002, publishing a demand notice in the Nanfang Daily on January 30, 2003, and sending a demand notice to the Construction Corporation by mail on December 1, 2003, were all unilateral demands for payment by the creditor after the expiry of the guarantee period and could not form a new guarantee relationship. Therefore, the Construction Corporation would no longer bear the guarantee liability for the USD 3,250,000 loan. With respect to the loan of USD 1,611,031.25, since the Guangzhou Office could not prove that the loan had been disbursed, the Raw Materials Company was not liable for repayment of the loan. Therefore, the Guangzhou Office's claim for the Construction Corporation to bear guarantee liability for this loan was not supported.

In summary, the Guangzhou Office's claim for the Raw Materials Company to repay the principal and interest of the USD 3,250,000 loan was supported. The Guangzhou Office's other claims were not supported due to insufficient evidence. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 10 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases Involving Assets Formed from the Acquisition, Management, and Disposal of Non-performing Loans of State-owned Banks by Financial Asset Management Companies, Article 32 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 26 of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 79 and 80 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 108 and 135 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 64 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court of first instance rendered the following judgment: 1. The Raw Materials Company shall, within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment, repay to the Guangzhou Office the loan principal of USD 3,250,000 and interest (interest during the loan term shall be calculated according to the interest rate stipulated in the contract; overdue penalty interest shall be calculated according to the penalty interest standard of the Bank of China for overdue foreign exchange loans). In case of delay in performance, execution shall be carried out in accordance with Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China; 2. The Guangzhou Office's other claims are dismissed. The court acceptance fee for the first instance is RMB 510,935.32, of which the Guangzhou Office shall bear RMB 170,311.78 and the Raw Materials Company shall bear RMB 340,623.54. The Guangzhou Office has prepaid RMB 255,468 in litigation fees, which will not be refunded. After offsetting, the Raw Materials Company shall directly pay RMB 85,156.22 to the Guangzhou Office when executing the judgment, and at the same time pay the litigation fee of RMB 255,467.32 to the court of first instance.

Guangzhou Office, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the court of first instance, filed an appeal to this Court, arguing: 1. The judgment of first instance found that the loan of USD 1,611,031.25 was not actually disbursed, thereby improperly discharging the joint liability for repayment that the Raw Materials Company should bear and the joint suretyship liability that the Construction Corporation should bear. The loan contract dated May 18, 1996, stipulating an amount of USD 1,611,031.25, had its loan disbursal obligation performed by the lender, Zhongshan Sub-branch of Bank of China. The reasons are: (A) Before the disbursal of this loan, the Raw Materials Company had submitted a loan application to Zhongshan Sub-branch, which, due to a shortage of funds, borrowed from a third party, Shanwei Sub-branch of China Construction Bank (hereinafter referred to as Shanwei Construction Bank) on May 10, 1995, forming an interbank lending agreement. Pursuant to the instructions of Zhongshan Sub-branch, Shanwei Construction Bank directly deposited the borrowed funds of USD 1.5 million into the account of the Raw Materials Company opened at Zhongshan Sub-branch. Upon maturity of this borrowing, because the Raw Materials Company failed to repay, Zhongshan Sub-branch was forced to repay the borrowing from Shanwei Construction Bank with its own funds, thereby creating the loan of USD 1,611,031.25 in dispute in this case. (B) In addition to evidence such as the interbank lending agreement and transfer vouchers, the above facts are also clearly recorded in a report dated May 7, 1996, from the Raw Materials Company. The report states: "In May 1995, the (Raw Materials Company) borrowed USD 1.5 million from Shanwei Construction Bank through Zhongshan Sub-branch. This loan was mainly used to purchase equipment such as elevators and air-conditioning systems for the company's properties." This record, on one hand, explains the background of this borrowing by the Raw Materials Company, and on the other hand, indicates the actual use of the loan. In this report, the Raw Materials Company also stated that "due to difficulties in capital recovery and the maturity of the original borrowing, we respectfully request your bank (Zhongshan Sub-branch) to assist in resolving this matter. The principal and interest total USD 1,611,031.25." This specific amount is entirely consistent with the amount paid by Zhongshan Sub-branch on behalf of the Raw Materials Company to Shanwei Construction Bank on May 14, 1996, the amount in the loan contract signed between Zhongshan Sub-branch and the Raw Materials Company, and the amount in the irrevocable letter of guarantee issued by the Construction Corporation to Zhongshan Sub-branch on May 18 of the same year. Together, these demonstrate that Zhongshan Sub-branch created a claim against the Raw Materials Company by repaying Shanwei Construction Bank on its behalf, and at the same time fulfilled its performance obligations under the loan contract (amount USD 1,611,031.25) signed on May 18 of the same year. (C) After the above loan became overdue, Zhongshan Sub-branch and Guangzhou Office carried out continuous collection efforts. Among them, on June 16, 1998, the Credit Business Section of Zhongshan Sub-branch issued a collection notice to the Raw Materials Company and the Construction Corporation, which were respectively signed and sealed by both companies, indicating acknowledgment; on September 29, 1999, Zhongshan Sub-branch again issued a collection notice to the Raw Materials Company and the Construction Corporation, and both companies signed and sealed again; on June 18, 2000, Zhongshan Sub-branch mailed a notice of assignment of creditor's rights to the above two companies, not only informing them of the assignment of the claim to Guangzhou Office but also making a demand for payment; on June 29, 2000, this was notarized by the Guangdong Provincial Notary Public Office; on September 22, 2000, Guangzhou Office and Zhongshan Sub-branch jointly issued a notice of assignment of creditor's rights to the Construction Corporation, demanding repayment, and on September 29, 2000, this was notarized by the Guangdong Provincial Notary Public Office; on March 15, 2002, and January 30, 2003, Guangzhou Office published collection notices in the Nanfang Daily, including demands against the Raw Materials Company and the Construction Corporation; on November 25, 2002, Guangzhou Office made another demand, notarized on December 12, 2002, by the Guangdong Provincial Notary Public Office; on December 1, 2003, Guangzhou Office sent another collection letter to the above two companies.

2. The judgment of first instance improperly found that the guarantee liability of the Construction Corporation for the loan of USD 3.25 million was discharged upon expiration of the guarantee period. The judgment of first instance held that since the guarantee period stipulated in the irrevocable letter of guarantee issued by the Construction Corporation was until the borrower had repaid the loan principal and interest in full, according to Article 32, Paragraph 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the PRC, this agreed guarantee period is deemed to be two years from the date on which the principal debt's performance period expires. In this case, that date is December 21, 1998. During this period, there was no evidence that Zhongshan Sub-branch had asserted its rights. Therefore, the guarantor could be discharged from guarantee liability. On September 29, 1999, the Construction Corporation affixed its seal to a notice issued by Zhongshan Sub-branch demanding assumption of guarantee liability, which constitutes a new provision of guarantee for the debt after the expiration of the guarantee period, forming a new guarantor relationship. Since no guarantee period was stipulated, according to the above judicial interpretation, the guarantee period should be deemed as six months after the maturity of the principal debt. After this period, the Construction Corporation should be discharged from guarantee liability.

In fact, whether before or after December 21, 1998, Zhongshan Sub-branch and Guangzhou Office had been continuously demanding payment from the Raw Materials Company and the Construction Corporation. Due to issues concerning the assignment of creditor's rights, there were omissions in the storage and transfer of relevant materials. After the judgment of first instance was rendered, upon joint review of materials with Zhongshan Sub-branch, a payment demand notice dated June 16, 1998, issued by Zhongshan Sub-branch to the Raw Materials Company and the Construction Corporation was found. The Raw Materials Company, as borrower, and the Construction Corporation, as guarantor, affixed their seals to confirm this payment demand notice. Therefore, the finding in the judgment of first instance that no claim was made within the guarantee period is not established. At the same time, the collection on September 29, 1999, was also a continuous collection by the creditor, rather than the establishment of a new guarantee relationship. Together with the subsequent collections on June 18, 2000, September 22, 2000, March 15, 2002, November 25, 2002, January 30, 2003, and December 1, 2003, these constitute compelling evidence that the creditor actively asserted its rights against the guarantor.

3. Regarding the liability of the guarantor under the loan contract of USD 1,611,031.25 disbursed on May 18, 1996. The judgment of first instance held that under this contract, due to a lack of evidence that the lender had fulfilled its loan disbursal obligation, the Raw Materials Company's repayment obligation was discharged, and consequently, the Construction Corporation's guarantee obligation was naturally discharged. According to the facts set forth in point 1 above, Zhongshan Sub-branch had already fulfilled its obligation to disburse this loan. The Raw Materials Company, as the principal debtor, bears an undeniable repayment obligation, and the Construction Corporation, as the guarantor, should assume joint suretyship liability.

In summary, the Guangzhou Office requested that the Raw Materials Company be ordered to repay the loan principal of USD 4,861,031.25 and corresponding interest and overdue liquidated damages to the Guangzhou Office; that the Construction Corporation be ordered to assume joint suretyship liability for the above debt; and that the Raw Materials Company and the Construction Corporation bear the case acceptance fees for the first and second instances.

The Raw Materials Company and the Construction Corporation did not submit written defense opinions.

In this second instance, in addition to confirming the facts found in the judgment of first instance, this Court further supplemented and found the following facts:

1. Regarding whether the loan of USD 1,611,031.25 was actually disbursed. In a report submitted to Zhongshan Sub-branch on May 7, 1996, the Raw Materials Company stated: In May 1995, the company borrowed USD 1.5 million from Shanwei Construction Bank through Zhongshan Sub-branch. This borrowing was mainly used to purchase equipment such as elevators and air-conditioning systems needed for the company's properties; due to factors such as macro-control, the company had difficulty recovering funds, and the original borrowing had matured. It sincerely requested the bank (Zhongshan Sub-branch) to assist in resolving this matter, with the principal and interest totaling USD 1,611,031.25; as the real estate market improved and sales funds were normally recovered, the company would repay the above USD 1,611,031.25 on time. During the second-instance cross-examination, the Guangzhou Office submitted to this Court: an Interbank Lending Contract signed on May 10, 1995, between Zhongshan Sub-branch and the third party Shanwei Construction Bank; a Report on Request to Book the Principal and Interest of the Original Interbank Borrowing from Shanwei Construction Bank of USD 1,611,031.25 under Account 741 of the Bank (hereinafter referred to as the Zhongshan Sub-branch Report) submitted by Zhongshan Sub-branch to the bank's leadership on May 13, 1996; and a remittance voucher of Zhongshan Sub-branch to China Construction Bank Guangdong Sub-branch through Bank of China Guangdong Sub-branch on May 14, 1996 (the voucher indicated: repayment of the interbank borrowing from Shanwei Construction Bank, and was stamped with the official seal of the Raw Materials Company). All of the above evidentiary materials were copies. The copy of the Interbank Lending Contract indicated: Zhongshan Sub-branch borrowed USD 1.5 million from Shanwei Construction Bank, with the borrowing period from May 11 of the same year to May 10, 1996. The Guangzhou Office had already submitted a copy of this Interbank Lending Contract to the court of first instance, but the court of first instance did not conduct cross-examination. The above-mentioned Zhongshan Sub-branch Report stated: The interbank borrowing of USD 1.5 million from Shanwei Construction Bank by Zhongshan Sub-branch, with interest of USD 111,031.25, totaling USD 1,611,031.25 in principal and interest, had matured. Shanwei Construction Bank had repeatedly called, under pressure from the provincial bank, demanding that our bank repay this borrowing as soon as possible. However, the user unit, the Raw Materials Company, was unable to repay on time for various reasons. It was proposed that our bank temporarily book the amount and then request a special resolution from the head office and the provincial bank.

Regarding the issue of the loan disbursal voucher, the Guangzhou Office stated that due to management reasons, when Zhongshan Sub-branch transferred the creditor's rights in this case, the transferred evidentiary materials did not include the disbursal voucher. However, considering other evidence in the case, it was sufficient to prove that Zhongshan Sub-branch had fulfilled its obligation to disburse the loan at that time.

2. Regarding the collection of the loans of USD 1,611,031.25 and USD 3.25 million. During the second-instance cross-examination, the Guangzhou Office submitted to this Court two Collection Notices issued by Zhongshan Sub-branch to the Raw Materials Company and the Construction Corporation demanding payment. The above two Collection Notices were dated June 16, 1998, with the demanded amounts being USD 1,611,031.25 and USD 3.25 million respectively. The Raw Materials Company and the Construction Corporation affixed their seals to the Collection Notices as borrower and guarantor, respectively. The Guangzhou Office used this to prove that its assertion of rights against the principal debtor, the Raw Materials Company, and the guarantor, the Construction Corporation, had not exceeded the two-year statute of limitations and the two-year guarantee period. After cross-examination by this Court in the second instance, the Raw Materials Company and the Construction Corporation acknowledged affixing their official seals to the Collection Notices but objected to the cross-examination on the grounds that the Guangzhou Office had only provided these evidentiary materials during the second instance, exceeding the time limit for evidence submission.

Opinion of the Court: The loan guarantee contracts signed on December 21, 1995, by and between Zhongshan Sub-branch, the Raw Materials Company, and the Construction Corporation, which respectively stipulated loan amounts of USD 2 million and USD 1.25 million, represented the true intent of the parties, did not violate prohibitive provisions of laws or administrative regulations, and should be recognized as legally valid. Zhongshan Sub-branch fulfilled its obligation to disburse the loans in accordance with the contracts. Upon maturity, the Raw Materials Company failed to repay the loans, and the Construction Corporation also failed to perform its guarantee obligation. The Raw Materials Company's actions constituted a breach of contract and should bear corresponding civil liability. The repayment date stipulated in the above loan contracts totaling USD 3.25 million was December 21, 1996. The statute of limitations for the claim arising from these loans should commence from the date the repayment period expired. Based on the facts found in this second instance, on June 16, 1998, Zhongshan Sub-branch made a demand for payment regarding the above USD 3.25 million loan to the Raw Materials Company and the Construction Corporation. Therefore, this should cause an interruption of the statute of limitations. The demand made by Zhongshan Sub-branch to the Raw Materials Company on September 29, 1999, constituted an assertion of rights within the statute of limitations period. The sealing of the Collection Notice for Overdue Loans by the Raw Materials Company constituted a confirmation of the debt within the statute of limitations period. The judgment of first instance held that the above action by the Raw Materials Company was a reconfirmation of the loan debt after the expiration of the statute of limitations period, and that the statute of limitations should be recalculated. This finding was erroneous and is corrected by this Court. However, the judgment of first instance's order that the Raw Materials Company repay the loan principal of USD 3.25 million and interest and overdue fine to the Guangzhou Office was not improper, and the Raw Materials Company did not appeal. Therefore, this Court affirms item 1 of the main text of the judgment of first instance.

There are two main points of contention in this second instance: First, whether the Construction Corporation should assume guarantee liability for the above USD 3.25 million; Second, whether the loan of USD 1,611,031.25 was disbursed and whether the Construction Corporation should assume guarantee liability.

1. Regarding whether the Construction Corporation should assume guarantee liability for the above USD 3.25 million. The reason the judgment of first instance ordered the Construction Corporation not to assume guarantee liability for the above loan was that the creditor had not asserted its rights against it within the guarantee period. During the second-instance cross-examination, the Guangzhou Office submitted to this Court two Collection Notices dated June 16, 1998, with demanded amounts of USD 1,611,031.25 and USD 3.25 million respectively, to prove that its assertion of rights against the principal debtor, the Raw Materials Company, and the guarantor, the Construction Corporation, had not exceeded the two-year statute of limitations and the two-year guarantee period. Although the Raw Materials Company and the Construction Corporation objected to the cross-examination of these evidentiary materials, they also acknowledged having affixed their seals to the Collection Notices as borrower and guarantor, respectively. This Court holds that since this is a second instance, this Court may decide to conduct cross-examination of evidentiary materials submitted by the parties in the second instance based on the circumstances of the case. The fact that the Raw Materials Company and the Construction Corporation objected to the cross-examination on the grounds that the Guangzhou Office had only provided these evidentiary materials during the second instance, exceeding the time limit for evidence submission, does not affect this Court's review and acceptance of these evidentiary materials based on the circumstances of the case. Since the Raw Materials Company and the Construction Corporation acknowledged affixing their official seals to the Collection Notices, the Collection Notices should be deemed genuine. The Guangzhou Office's assertion of rights against the principal debtor, the Raw Materials Company, and the guarantor, the Construction Corporation, did not exceed the two-year statute of limitations and the two-year guarantee period. The Construction Corporation should assume joint liability for the principal and interest of the above USD 3.25 million loan.

2. Regarding whether the loan of USD 1,611,031.25 was disbursed and whether the Construction Corporation should assume guarantee liability. Although there is no direct evidence in this case proving that Zhongshan Sub-branch disbursed the USD 1.5 million loan (later expressed as USD 1,611,031.25 including interest) to the Raw Materials Company directly or through the third party, Shanwei Construction Bank, based on the facts found in this second instance, namely the report of the Raw Materials Company applying for the loan from Zhongshan Sub-branch, the Interbank Lending Contract signed between Zhongshan Sub-branch and Shanwei Construction Bank, the Zhongshan Sub-branch Report, the repayment voucher from Zhongshan Sub-branch to Shanwei Construction Bank, and the multiple Collection Notices issued by Zhongshan Sub-branch to the Raw Materials Company and the Construction Corporation, these pieces of circumstantial evidence are interlinked, forming a chain of evidence sufficient to prove that Zhongshan Sub-branch had disbursed the loan and held this claim. Therefore, the Raw Materials Company should bear the repayment obligation for this loan, and the Construction Corporation should assume joint liability.

In summary, regarding the guarantee liability for the USD 3.25 million loan, because the Guangzhou Office failed to provide evidence during the first instance, the judgment of first instance ordering the Construction Corporation not to assume guarantee liability was not improper. During the second instance, the Guangzhou Office submitted two new pieces of evidence to prove that its assertion of rights against the principal debtor, the Raw Materials Company, and the guarantor, the Construction Corporation, did not exceed the statute of limitations and the guarantee period. This Court, after cross-examination, accepted the above evidentiary materials and rendered a judgment that the Construction Corporation should assume joint liability for the above loan. Article 38 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Reforming the Methods of Civil and Economic Trial stipulates: "If the people's court of second instance changes the original judgment or remands the case for retrial based on new evidence submitted by a party, it shall specify in the judgment or ruling the confirmation of the new evidence, and it shall not be deemed an error in the judgment of first instance." Therefore, this Court's revision of the adjudication of guarantee liability for the above loan should not be considered an error in the judgment of first instance. However, regarding the adjudication of liability for the USD 1,611,031.25 loan, it should be determined that the judgment of first instance had unclear findings of fact and improper adjudication of liability, which are corrected by this Court. The grounds of appeal of the Guangzhou Office are established and are supported by this Court. Pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Items (1) and (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, this Court renders the following judgment:

1. Affirming the part of item 1 of the main text of the Civil Judgment (2004) Yue Gao Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 1 of the Guangdong High People's Court that orders Zhongshan Industrial Raw Materials Company to repay the loan principal of USD 3.25 million and interest and overdue fine to China Orient Asset Management Corporation, Guangzhou Office (interest during the loan period shall be calculated at the rate stipulated in the contract, and the overdue fine shall be calculated according to the Bank of China's standards for overdue foreign exchange loans);

2. Reversing item 2 of the main text of the Civil Judgment (2004) Yue Gao Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 1 of the Guangdong High People's Court;

3. Zhongshan Industrial Raw Materials Company shall repay the loan principal of USD 1,611,031.25 and interest (calculated from May 15, 1996, until the date of full repayment, at the interest rate of the Bank of China for foreign exchange loans of the same period) to China Orient Asset Management Corporation, Guangzhou Office;

4. Zhongshan Urban and Rural Construction Development Corporation shall assume joint liability for the payment obligations of Zhongshan Industrial Raw Materials Company to China Orient Asset Management Corporation, Guangzhou Office, as determined in items 1 and 3 of the main text of this judgment;

5. Zhongshan Urban and Rural Construction Development Corporation shall have the right to seek recourse from Zhongshan Industrial Raw Materials Company after assuming joint liability.

The above payment obligations shall be performed within fifteen days from the day following the date of service of this judgment. In case of overdue performance, it shall be handled according to Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC.

The case acceptance fee for the first instance is RMB 510,935.32, to be borne by Zhongshan Industrial Raw Materials Company. The case acceptance fee for the second instance is RMB 255,468, to be borne respectively by Zhongshan Industrial Raw Materials Company and Zhongshan Urban and Rural Construction Development Corporation, each in the amount of RMB 127,734.

This judgment is final.
